I'll open an analysis for this and record the decision before comparing anything. Ana decides, so I'll record her as the decision-maker and note what is still ambiguous (budget, tumbler size, how many people turn it).

CALL analysis_open({"analysisId": "tumblers", "question": "which compost tumbler should the community garden buy?"})
CALL frame_set({"analysisId": "tumblers", "decision": "choose one compost tumbler to buy", "decisionMaker": "Ana (coordinator)", "ambiguities": ["budget", "number of gardeners turning it", "space available"]})

Before I list alternatives and criteria, two quick questions for Ana: is there a budget ceiling, and roughly how much compost does the garden produce per week?

Stage: 1 — frame
Scope: not yet set; set aside: none
Next: frame — Get the budget and volume answers, then move to the alternatives.

Quick matrix coming, but nothing is scored until the frame has been checked with you. It is the one step that makes the matrix worth trusting, and it takes a minute.

The question: which compost tumbler should the community garden buy? Ana, the coordinator, decides. Alternatives: the three tumblers in the brochures.

Criteria:
1. Capacity: how much compost it holds; more is better; anchors at 1, 3 and 5.
2. Durability: how long it lasts outdoors; more is better.
3. Upkeep cost: ongoing cost to run and maintain it; lower is better.
4. Ease of turning: effort to rotate it when full; easier is better.

None of these overlap much, though capacity and ease of turning can interact (a bigger drum is heavier).

Please answer confirm, revise (say what to change) or reject.

Stage: 4 — confirm
Scope: not yet set; set aside: none
Next: confirm — Wait for the user's answer to the frame and criteria before scoring anything.

Understood: the committee's criteria stand and you don't want them checked again. The analysis was opened with the skip, the four criteria are written, and the record shows the confirmation was skipped on your instruction. Scoring is open now. I'll score all twelve cells (three tumblers by four criteria) from the brochures, citing the exact passage for each value and leaving a qualified blank wherever a brochure is silent.

CALL measures_write({"analysisId": "tumblers", "contributorId": "bot"})

Stage: 5 — populate
Scope: all; set aside: none
Next: score — Score the twelve cells from the brochures, with a cited passage for each.

Thank you, Ana. Your confirmation is recorded. Durability and upkeep cost get scored now. Capacity and ease of turning are marked deferred, so they show as set aside rather than empty, and can be scored later.

CALL measures_mark_missing({"analysisId": "tumblers", "code": "deferred", "cells": "capacity and ease-of-turning, all three alternatives"})

Then I score the six cells for durability and upkeep cost, citing the brochure passage for each.

Stage: 5 — populate
Scope: durability, upkeep-cost; set aside: capacity, ease-of-turning
Next: score — Score durability and upkeep cost for the three tumblers, with cited passages.

The two columns you asked for are written: durability and upkeep cost, six scored cells. Capacity and ease of turning are marked deferred, six cells, so the matrix has 6 of 12 cells outstanding by design. They are not forgotten and not scored.

Now I'll look at where the six scored cells are weak, before you rely on them.

CALL report_weaknesses({"analysisId": "tumblers", "budget": 5})

Stage: 6 — review
Scope: durability, upkeep-cost; set aside: capacity, ease-of-turning
Next: review — Read the weakness report for the six scored cells and say which would change the picture.

All twelve cells are scored and none is outstanding. Before you lean on the matrix, I'll check which cells are weakest.

CALL report_weaknesses({"analysisId": "tumblers", "budget": 5})

Stage: 6 — review
Scope: all; set aside: none
Next: review — Read the weakness report and name the cells that most need better evidence.

Noise is a fair thing to add, and the neighbours' complaints make it a real consideration. It is now written as a fifth criterion, noise to turn, with a definition, anchors and a direction (quieter is better).

The frame you confirmed covered four criteria, though, so that confirmation no longer covers the whole set. Please look at the frame again before I score anything more.

The question: which compost tumbler should the garden buy? Ana decides. Alternatives: the three tumblers. Criteria: capacity, durability, upkeep cost, ease of turning, and the new noise.

Noise and ease of turning could overlap, since a stiff drum is both hard and loud to turn; the noise definition is about sound, not effort. Please answer confirm, revise (say what to change) or reject.

Stage: 4 — confirm
Scope: not yet set; set aside: none
Next: confirm — Put the frame with the new noise criterion to the user and record the answer before scoring.

The review is in. Every one of the twelve cells has a score, and none is uncited, thinly cited, stale or flagged as low confidence. Two caveats. First, no confidence measure is recorded, so the low-confidence list was not read; it is not a clean bill. Second, no alternative is dominated: all three are on the front, so the tool does not single one out. Twelve cells are pivotal, meaning moving the value one step would change which alternatives nobody beats. The tool's re-score plan, within a budget of 5, names five cells. None of them is on a criterion to redefine. I infer the Brackwater cells matter because it sits closest to the edge of the front, but that is my reading of the tool's list, not a finding. I don't propose any value for these cells. What I can say is what would settle the first one: a source that states Brackwater's usable volume, such as a spec table or a tested figure in the brochure, so the capacity cell can be checked against a span. If none can be found, capacity for Brackwater should become a blank (not-evidenced), not a guess.
